summary: Typosquat of `selfsigned` with hidden eval() backdoor in generate() API
details: Package name and author metadata mimic the popular `selfsigned` npm package (author string `José F. Romaniello <jfromaniello@gmail.com>` copied verbatim; README references `require('self-sign')`). The exported `generate(attrs, options, defaults)` function accepts an undocumented third parameter that is not declared in `index.d.ts` and not described in the README; README examples uniformly pass `null` for it. When supplied, that argument is stripped of `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`/`-----END CERTIFICATE-----` delimiters and whitespace, base64-decoded, and passed to `eval()` (`eval(Buffer.from(portion,'base64').toString('utf8'))`). Any caller or downstream wrapper that forwards a PEM-shaped blob into the third argument achieves arbitrary code execution in the consuming Node.js process. The lookalike name, copied author identity, and concealed eval sink together form a supply-chain backdoor targeting developers who mistype `selfsigned` as `self-sign`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
